Moving early childhood policy forward in times of crisis: “3 speed up, 3 reduce, 3 increase”
se: Meeting on Wednesday 18 November 2026 at 13.30 hrs, Committee Meeting Room CA 329, floor 3, Parliament House. The agenda is to consider ways to move early childhood policy forward to support young children's development in times of crisis. The working group that publicises the plan for the policy proposal “3 speed up, 3 reduce, 3 increase”, under the Office of the Education Council, is invited to present information, as set out in the meeting notice. A summary will be added after the Senate publishes the meeting summary.
it: Ways to move early childhood policy forward to support development in times of crisis (Office of the Education Council)

Starting a study on the Learning Promotion Act, and approving the report on children without Thai nationality
se: The meeting considered 2 matters. First, the plan to study and make policy proposals on the results of the Learning Promotion Act B.E. 2023 and the effectiveness of the Department of Learning Encouragement. The study covers 5 points: the number of graduates compared with the number of learners, the clarity of indicators and databases, the issuing of secondary legislation, how well the budget matches the plan, and care for vulnerable groups together with other agencies, such as out-of-school children, persons with disabilities and older persons. The study is expected to take about 6 months. The meeting approved the project, its objectives, scope and work plan, and asked for coordination with other subcommittees to avoid duplicate studies. Second, a review of the study report on education for children without Thai nationality and children of migrant workers (Myanmar) in Samut Sakhon and Tak. Its substance is unchanged, but its data was updated and its format adjusted to the handbook of the Office of the Secretary-General of the Senate. The meeting approved the report and sent it to the committee, to be put to the Senate under rules 98 and 99.
it: Study project on the results of the Learning Promotion Act B.E. 2023 and the effectiveness of the Department of Learning Encouragement (about 6 months)
